pitch_detail.notes: Reach the start notch by scrambling around the bergschrunds, about 100 ft above the base of the pyramid. The first pitch is class 3 on solid rock with good cracks for gear up to about 1.5 in; the next two are easy 4th class with horns for slings or terrain belays.
Low 5th class moves on quality rock to the summit; about 5.3 with selective route-finding; holding strictly to the crest adds two steps near 5.6 and 5.7.

review.changed: Wrote P1-3 only (terrain split between class 3 and easy 4th, horns, crack protection, bergschrund scramble to the notch). P4-6 not in batch. Second page (SummitPost Southeast Corner) returned 403, so only one full page read.
review.other_findings: Search snippets disagree on difficulty of the upper pitches (5.3-5.4 vs a 5.6 report); the stored 5.6/5.7 crest-steps note is not confirmed by the page read.

pitch_detail.notes: Long forest/subalpine trail; the modern approach adds a closed-road walk/bike before the historic trailhead.

Mostly above treeline: follow the ridge above the flats until it steepens, then traverse right across a south-facing slope to the gap. Easy trail in summer; wet slides and cornices are a concern in winter and spring. The maintained trail effectively ends at the gap.
pitch_detail.pitch: Goat Flats to Tin Can Gap

pitch_detail.notes: Ice axe and crampons required. Cross or skirt a small, steep snowfield on the north side of the ridge, cross onto the south face, and come back north at the top of the glacier; late in summer a moat between ice and rock can be followed. A slip here slides about 200 ft into rock, and some parties rope up. Ends at a snowfield below the summit rock.
pitch_detail.pitch: Tin Can Gap across the Queest-Alb Glacier edge

pitch_detail.notes: Three fixed ladders (rebar/timber anchored) gain the blasted summit block and L-4 lookout cabin at ~6,850 ft.

review.changed: Wrote both boxes from two pages; no lengths stated for these segments so none added. Mixed winter ski-report conditions limited to a short hazard note.
review.other_findings: Stored approach says Goat Flats to the gap is about 2 miles; neither page gives that segment distance. Stored pitch label for the glacier box says crevasse hazard; pages show conditions vary a lot by year.
